text.title: Card Sorting Worked Example
text.summary: One end-to-end worked example of Card Sorting producing a valid spec artefact, anonymised for portability. Concrete open and closed sort examples demonstrating result interpretation and decision rules.

step.name: trigger
step.text: Engagement onboarded; the Card Sorting methodology was selected after Applies-If was satisfied (named owner Ruslan Faion, downstream consumer named in engagement charter, source-of-truth pinned in docs/).

step.name: apply-rules
step.text: Walked the rules from 01-core-rules.xml. Most rules passed on first review; one required a follow-up because a required citation was missing. Captured the gap, patched, re-ran.

step.name: produce
step.text: Filled templates/card-sorting.json with all required fields per the JSON Schema; emitted artefact_id with date; signed off by the engagement owner.

step.name: validate
step.text: Ran scripts/validate-card-sorting.py --file <path>; validator returned 0; smoke-test fixture in templates/_smoke-test.json also passed.

step.name: handover
step.text: Artefact registered with the downstream consumer; entry added to the engagement decision log; version locked at 1.1.0.

example.note: Content: e-commerce product categories. Results: 15 of 20 users grouped "Laptops" and "Desktops" together (75% agreement — above 70% threshold, definite grouping). Users named this category "Computers" not "Computing Devices." "Tablets" split: 8 users with computers, 7 with phones (40% each — ambiguous, needs further testing). Decision: Create "Computers" category with that label; run tree test to validate tablet placement.

Categories: Electronics, Home, Clothing. Results: Smart Watch → Electronics 85% (clear); Fitness Tracker → Electronics 70% (clear); Heated Blanket → Home 55%, Electronics 40% (ambiguous — below 70% in both). Decision: Heated Blanket needs re-categorization research; consider dual-listing or a new category.
